To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed a secure fingerprint biometric system based on the use of a family of symmetric cryptographic hash functions and that our approach does not depend on any assumption on the location of core and delta.

(1) the use of the proposed hash functions in a biometric system does not degrade the system performance significantly; (2) the use of these hash functions in a hybrid system that combines the minutia and the hash spaces can significantly improve the system performance; (3) these hash functions can be used in a cancellable biometric system that can be used in conjunction with a traditional minutia-based system; (4) the proposed hash functions can be applied to other biometrics such as iris

the use of symmetric hash functions for biometric authentication is possible and that the EER achieved by our system using symmetric hash functions is very close to that achieved by plain matching in the original minutia space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of secure and robust biometrics based authentication system for fingerprint.
developing an effective and secure fingerprint biometric system.
the development of a new fingerprint identification system that can be used in secure biometric applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
The proposed method of hashing the minutia and performing matching in the hash space is a viable solution for securing biometric databases.
the proposed method of hashing minutia is very promising.

1) The performance of the hybrid system is very close to that of the plain minutia matching, 2) The symmetric hash functions used are very robust against attacks, and 3) The symmetric hash function based fingerprint identification system does not depend on singular points or pre-alignment of the fingerprints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented a novel method of secure fingerprint identification and verification that is based on symmetric hashing.
we have shown that hashing minutia is feasible and can be used in a cancellable fingerprint system with very low error rates.
the proposed system has an EER that is close to the performance achieved by plain minutia matching, while at the same time it is secure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of symmetric hash functions for fingerprint biometrics is feasible.
it is possible to develop a cancellable system that does not depend on a pre-alignment of the fingerprint templates.
the performance of the proposed system is very close to that of plain minutia matching.
